reason: The cold cloud is moving inward, so bringing it to the dense central disk may help form the central stars.
expectation: I expect the disk material to join the central gas and possibly contribute to a new star-forming gathering.

alternatives.reason: The returning shell also seems relevant, but I want to follow the cold cloud inward first.

effect: The disk's lost material helped form new central stars; I can now follow their effect on nearby gas.
reaction: It's satisfying to see material that missed the planets contribute to new stars.
reason: Combining the new stars with the central clouds directly addresses what the stars do to their remaining gas.
expectation: I expect their radiation or outflows to heat or disperse some of the cloud.

alternatives.reason: The returning shell is also worth following, but the new stars offer a direct next step.

effect: The central stars heated and drove some remaining gas above the disk, completing that goal. The returning shell is the only available gameplay action.
reaction: The contrast between the bright nursery and faint outflow is interesting.
reason: I'll follow the returning shell into the extended gas; it's the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the shell material to mix or gather with gas in the returning galaxy, though its eventual fate is unclear.

effect: The returning shell collided with extended gas, sending some material inward toward the centre and completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The contrast with freely passing stars ties the encounter back to the larger story.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the small disk's lost material into new central stars was satisfying: matter that missed the planets contributed to another generation of lights.

leastWorthwhile.text: The returning shell was the only available action at that point, so the choice itself was less engaging, even though its result added context.

surprise.text: The returning gas could take different inward paths, potentially joining central star-forming gas or the flow around the black hole.

arbitrary.text: None felt arbitrary; each action had a clear connection to a goal or the returning material.

continue.text: Yes. I'd be curious to follow the returning gas and see how the shared galaxy develops, though the forced final action was less engaging.
